note: Architectural interpretations from photographic references; not documentary photographs.

assets.prompt: Create a sophisticated minimalist architectural background for a personal academic portfolio website, using the supplied photographs as visual references. This is one asset in a coherent four-page art direction. Wide landscape 16:9 composition, ideally 2560 pixels wide. Quiet contemporary architectural visualization with subtle matte and translucent materials, very soft natural light, clean precise geometry, delicate tonal depth. Elegant and calm, neither a photograph with a white overlay nor a wireframe diagram. Preserve the building's identifiable structural character while removing incidental detail. Place the strongest recognizable architecture in the UPPER RIGHT and right two-thirds, extending off the top and right edges. The leftmost 35% must remain almost empty pale background for dark heading text, with a gradual gentle transition, and the bottom 25% should dissolve into a nearly uniform pale background. Main architecture should remain recognizable and moderately distinct at reduced size. Never include text, labels, logos, signage, UI, lettering, people, cars, decorative unrelated objects, or watermarks. No glossy plastic toy model, no generic sci-fi city, no dramatic black shadows. All visual detail should be concentrated at the upper/right edges to allow legible text and translucent content cards on top. Full opaque background, no transparency. ABOUT / KYOTO STATION by Hiroshi Hara. Distill the enormous steel-and-glass atrium: sweeping roof lattice, a deep central canyon perspective, slender bridge and nested geometric frames. Architecture occupies the right side and top edge, with fine steel grid lines at human architectural scale. One coherent perspective, not a collage. The structural vault and vanishing point must clearly resemble these photographs. Palette pearl silver, icy blue, pale blue-gray, tiny hints of muted cyan. Ambient high-tech atmosphere achieved with structural precision and translucent glazing, not neon or saturated gradients. Flat background near #f3f6f8; atmospheric roof members in muted #a1b6c3 with a few #6c899a accents. Keep the left central region blank and light.

RESEARCH / PHILIPS PAVILION, Brussels 1958, by Le Corbusier and Iannis Xenakis. Extract the distinctive soaring, asymmetrical warped thin-shell building from the reference photographs: multiple pointed peaks, steep outward leaning spire, saddle surfaces and small triangular entrance. A coherent abstract architectural relief of the actual pavilion rather than a generic cone. Arrange its main mass toward upper right, projecting into open pale space. Subtle long linear seams articulate the ruled surfaces; smooth pearl material with a restrained frosted translucent edge. Quiet mathematical futurism, not space scenery. Palette near-white #f5f4f8, soft lavender-gray #c7c5d7 and muted slate-violet #8d8da8. Keep a few crisp silhouette edges and the internal shell shaded softly, while left third stays blank and pale. No trees, crowds, exhibition context, scaffolding or other buildings.

PROJECTS / LE CORBUSIER: RONCHAMP + LA TOURETTE. Translate Ronchamp's unmistakable heavy curved roof floating over a chalk-white curving wall, its irregular small punched openings, and La Tourette's disciplined concrete facade rhythm and colored light openings into ONE coherent minimalist architectural composition on the right side. Let Ronchamp's sculptural roof and wall be the dominant recognizable form; let an adjacent low rectangular translucent/concrete plane carry La Tourette's unequal vertical rhythm and one red aperture, one blue aperture, and one small ochre-yellow light plane. Colors sparse, like carefully positioned pigments within the architecture, not colorful blocks scattered around. Refined smooth chalk and pale warm concrete rather than grungy brutalism. Palette background #f6f3ed, chalk #eeeae0, warm concrete #c9c4b8, muted cobalt #456b90, brick-red #b65b47, ochre #ba9a50. Cast very soft daylight shadows, lots of empty space, no vegetation or photographic grain. Architecture as elevated geometric design study; keep left central region nearly blank.

BLOG / HANGZHOU NATIONAL ARCHIVES OF PUBLICATIONS AND CULTURE by Wang Shu and Lu Wenyu. Retain the ACTUAL contemporary Chinese architecture from the references: long low roof and very slender dark horizontal eave, structural timber under the eave, tall celadon-green pivoting screen panels with tiled relief surfaces, quiet stone courtyard and an abstract shallow water reflection. Arrange a partial pavilion facade across the upper right, with repeated offset screen planes revealing layered empty courtyards, and a subtle horizontal reflection underneath that fades to ivory. Emphasize long horizontals, framed empty space and Song-dynasty restraint through a modern architectural rendering. No generic pagodas, curved temple roofs, lanterns, mountains, calligraphy, people, decorative Asian icons, or ink-painting scenery. Palette rice-paper ivory #f4f4ec, celadon #8ea99a, deep pale moss #779384, stone gray #c8ccc1 and sparse ink #56635c. Clean surfaces with extremely subtle texture, soft mist-free daylight; keep architecture recognizable and left central space blank.
